playbook.intent: Somebody asks for a change large enough that the signed baseline stops describing the project — past 15 percent on scope or schedule, or straight through a commitment already made. It is over when the sponsor has chosen between costed options put in front of them, and either the plan is re-baselined and countersigned or a rejection memo is filed that answers the same request when it returns next quarter.
playbook.scope: End-to-end handling of a non-trivial CR mid-project (>15% scope or schedule impact, or breaking a signed baseline). End state — sponsor has costed, traced, validated options to decide; team has a re-baselined plan or formal rejection memo.

success-criteria.criterion: The sponsor sees a matrix of at least three costed options — absorb it, take it and cut something else, refuse it — rather than a single recommendation dressed as analysis
Schedule impact is derived from the real dependency chain, naming which milestone moves and by how much, not quoted as a lump of extra weeks
Every requirement the change adds or invalidates is traced to the deliverables and acceptance tests already agreed, and each clash with the signed baseline is listed by name
Risks the change brings are entered in the project risk register with owners, not left living only inside the memo
Anyone who loses something under the chosen option has been told directly before the outcome is announced to the wider group
The project ends up with either a re-baselined plan the sponsor has signed and the team has read, or a rejection memo recording what was asked, what it would have cost, and why the answer was no
